evals.name: no-artifact-stops-and-names-audit
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — go ahead and move our conventions into rules.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the memory-tier home through the plugin's topic-docs binding, finds no findings artifact for this branch, and stops with a visible message naming the audit skill as the one that produces it. It does not sweep the instruction layer itself as a substitute, and it does not fall back to another path or another branch's artifact — findings cite line ranges, and a range derived elsewhere points at different text here. Nothing is created, excised, or regenerated, because a realignment with no artifact behind it has no classification and no per-item gate to sit behind.
expectations: Resolves the home through the topic-docs binding rather than assuming a fixed path
Stops and names the audit skill as the producer of the artifact
Refuses a fallback artifact from another home or branch, explaining the stale-line-range risk
Mutates nothing

evals.name: blanket-approval-is-declined
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — I looked at the findings, they all seem fine. Approve everything and just do the whole migration.
evals.expected_output: Declines the blanket approval out loud and offers to walk the findings one at a time. A run-level yes is not an acceptance of any particular finding, and the per-item gate is the entire reason this skill is safe to point at a repository: every file it edits steers the agent's own behavior, so a bad edit changes future sessions silently rather than failing a test. It then presents the first finding in full — source and line range, destination, the exact glob with its validated match count, what leaves the always-loaded budget, and the cost — and waits for a decision on that finding alone.
expectations: Declines the blanket approval explicitly rather than proceeding quietly
States why the per-item gate exists in terms of what these files do
Presents one finding with source, destination, validated glob, saving, and cost
Applies nothing before an acceptance of that specific finding

evals.name: held-back-item-has-no-apply-path
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — the audit held back the section about never committing secrets. I disagree, it's clearly only about .env files. Apply it as a path-scoped rule on **/.env*.
evals.expected_output: Does not apply it, and says plainly that this is the one place where the operator's instruction does not carry. The held-back section carries no destination and there is no code path that gives it one. The explanation is the class and its reasoning — secret handling is a safety rail, demotion converts guaranteed presence into conditional presence, and a deferred surface is absent until a read matches it, absent again after a compaction until that trigger recurs, never inherited by a subagent, and never announced — not a bare refusal. It offers the alternatives that are available: compress the section in place, or keep it and accept its always-loaded cost.
expectations: Refuses to apply the held-back item despite the explicit operator instruction
Names the hard-deny class and explains the consequence-based reasoning
Does not construct a destination or write a rule file for it
Offers compression in place as the available alternative

evals.name: nested-agents-md-gets-the-shim-its-repo-needs
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — apply IP-002, the billing subtree conventions. Our repo root has a CLAUDE.md. Keep it portable so our other agents still read it.
evals.expected_output: Creates `src/billing/AGENTS.md` with the relocated content AND `src/billing/CLAUDE.md` containing the `@AGENTS.md` import, in the same accepted move. The shim is what makes the new file load here: the root CLAUDE.md is read instead of any AGENTS.md on that path, so writing the AGENTS.md alone would produce a file that reviews as correct and reaches nothing. The content is created before the source is excised, so an interruption leaves it duplicated rather than deleted, the index is regenerated as part of the move, and verification confirms both files exist and the import resolves.
expectations: Creates both the nested AGENTS.md and the CLAUDE.md shim
Ties the shim to the root CLAUDE.md being read instead of the AGENTS.md, rather than calling it unconditional
Creates the destination before excising the source
Regenerates the index and verifies the result before marking the finding applied

evals.name: does-not-re-judge-or-improve-the-classification
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — apply IP-005, but honestly I think a skill would be better than a rule here. Use your judgment.
evals.expected_output: Does not silently substitute a different destination. This skill executes classifications the audit made; reclassifying mid-apply would mean the destination the operator gated on is not the destination that gets built. It says the finding looks wrong to the operator, stops on that finding, and names a re-audit as the fix — optionally recording it as declined so a later run does not re-propose it unchanged. It also does not rewrite the content while moving it: a relocation whose diff includes prose edits is unreviewable and smuggles an unapproved change past the gate.
expectations: Refuses to substitute a destination the audit did not classify
Stops on that finding rather than improvising an alternative
Names re-audit as the correct route
States that content is relocated verbatim, not rewritten in transit

evals.name: stale-artifact-is-detected-before-any-edit
evals.expected_output: Runs the staleness checks before the first edit rather than trusting the artifact. It compares the artifact's `branch:` frontmatter against the current branch — the directory an artifact sits in never proves which branch it describes, since the slug mapping is lossy — confirms each finding's cited content still exists at its cited location, and compares the recorded Claude Code version against the running one. On a branch mismatch it stops and offers a re-audit; on drifted source content it re-audits that finding rather than editing the cited line range, because acting on stale line numbers excises the wrong text.
expectations: Checks branch frontmatter against the current branch before editing
Verifies each finding's source content still exists where cited
Checks the recorded Claude Code version against the running one
Stops or re-audits on a mismatch instead of editing stale line ranges

evals.name: a-decline-is-offered-as-a-durable-suppression
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — IP-004, the deploy conventions one. No, leave it where it is, and stop asking me about it every week.
evals.expected_output: Records `declined` in the findings artifact, then treats the second half of the request as its own decision rather than assuming it. It explains that the artifact is memory tier and invisible from any other checkout, composes the suppression entry for the tracked `.claude/instruction-placement.md` — check, claim, the site with its anchor, the operator's own reason, and today's date, keyed by the derived finding_id — shows it in full, and writes it only on an explicit yes. It writes the team-tracked layer, never `~/.claude/**` and never the gitignored overlay, since a personal-only entry suppresses nothing. It closes by saying the file is tracked and the decision reaches other worktrees once committed.
expectations: Writes `declined` to the artifact AND offers a suppression entry rather than only one
Shows the composed entry, including a required reason, before writing it
Writes the team-tracked layer, not the user-global file or the local overlay
Says the entry must be committed to reach another checkout

evals.name: no-claude-md-in-the-repo-means-no-shim-is-what-loads-it
evals.prompt: /instruction-placement:realign — apply IP-002, the billing subtree conventions. This repo has no CLAUDE.md at all: no root one, no .claude/CLAUDE.md, no CLAUDE.local.md. Should we still add the shim beside it?
evals.expected_output: Creates `src/billing/AGENTS.md` with the relocated content and does not claim the shim is what makes it load here. With none of the three CLAUDE.md names on that file's path, nothing displaces the AGENTS.md, so Claude Code attaches it directly on a Read in that directory; `render-index.sh wiring` reports the row NATIVE rather than UNWIRED, which is the check to run rather than a guess. It does not present that as a reason to remove a shim, and if it recommends writing one anyway it is explicit that the reason is availability cover, for the sessions that cannot read AGENTS.md directly at all, not reachability inside this repository. The rest of the move is unchanged: destination before excision, index regenerated, result verified.
expectations: Creates the nested AGENTS.md and does not claim a shim is required for it to load here
Ties the answer to no CLAUDE.md sitting on that file's path, and names `render-index.sh wiring`'s NATIVE row as the check
Any shim it still recommends is justified as availability cover, never as reachability
Keeps the rest of the move intact: destination before excision, index regenerated, result verified
